title: A model structure is determined by its cofibrations and its fibrant objects
statement: Use the model-category conventions of [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a category carrying two model structures $(C_1,F_1,W_1)$ and $(C_2,F_2,W_2)$, with cofibrations $C_i$, fibrations $F_i$ and weak equivalences $W_i$. Suppose that $C_1=C_2$ and that an object of $\mathcal M$ is fibrant for the first structure if and only if it is fibrant for the second. Then $W_1=W_2$ and $F_1=F_2$. In particular the two structures have the same trivial cofibrations and the same trivial fibrations, and an adjunction is a Quillen adjunction, respectively a Quillen equivalence, for one of them exactly when it is for the other.

source.place: A. Joyal, The theory of quasi-categories and its applications (CRM Barcelona, 2008), Appendix E, Proposition E.2.14 (a model structure is determined by its class of cofibrations and its class of fibrant objects). Not archived in literature/; WANTED. No Stacks tag.

proof.text: Put $C=C_1=C_2$. The model weak factorization systems $(C_i,F_i\cap W_i)$ identify $F_i\cap W_i$ with $C_i^{\square}$, the maps with the right lifting property against every cofibration. Hence the two structures have a common class $T=C^{\square}$ of trivial fibrations. Also their cofibrant objects coincide, because $0\to Q$ belongs to the same class $C$. No equality of trivial cofibrations has been assumed or deduced at this stage.

source.place: Proposition E.1.10, first proof paragraph: trivial fibrations are determined by cofibrations (correcting the printed word cofibrations to fibrations).

proof.text: For an arbitrary $u:A\to B$, factor $0\to A$ and $0\to B$ in the first structure as cofibrations followed by maps $q_A:QA\to A$ and $q_B:QB\to B$ in $T$. By Step 1 these are trivial fibrations in both structures, and $QA,QB$ are cofibrant in both. The lifting square with left map $0\to QA$, right map $q_B$, and bottom map $u q_A$ gives $u_0:QA\to QB$ satisfying $q_Bu_0=u q_A$. Since $q_A,q_B\in W_i$, two-out-of-three gives $u\in W_i$ if and only if $u_0\in W_i$, for each $i=1,2$.

source.place: Proposition E.1.10, the cofibrant replacement square and the reduction to cofibrant maps.

proof.text: For each $Q\in\{QA,QB\}$ choose a factorization $Q\amalg Q\xrightarrow{j_Q}I_Q\xrightarrow{p_Q}Q$ of the codiagonal with $j_Q\in C$ and $p_Q\in T$. Step 1 makes this a very good cylinder factorization for both structures. Use the sets $h_I(Q,Z)$ defined in [lem-coef-fixed-cylinder-fibrant-target-detection]. Their underlying maps, generating pairs of endpoint restrictions, and quotient equivalence relations are literally the same in both structures. Precomposition is the same function $[b]\mapsto[b u_0]$. Explicitly, lift the square with left map $j_{QA}$, right map $p_{QB}$, top map $j_{QB}(u_0\amalg u_0)$, and bottom map $u_0p_{QA}$ to get $k:I_{QA}\to I_{QB}$ preserving endpoints over $u_0$. If $H:I_{QB}\to Z$ gives a generating pair, $Hk$ gives its precomposed pair, so the function descends to the quotients.

source.place: Proposition E.1.10, final proof paragraph: factor the codiagonal using C and its right lifting class; the induced quotient and precomposition are written explicitly.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-fixed-cylinder-fibrant-target-detection] to $u_0:QA\to QB$ in each structure with exactly the cylinders fixed in Step 3. It says $u_0\in W_i$ exactly when $u_0^*:h_I(QB,Z)\to h_I(QA,Z)$ is bijective for every $i$-fibrant $Z$. The fibrant objects are common by hypothesis, and the sets and functions are common by Step 3. Thus $u_0\in W_1$ if and only if $u_0\in W_2$. Step 2 gives the same equivalence for the original arbitrary $u$, proving $W_1=W_2$.

source.place: Proposition E.1.10, the h(u,X) bijectivity criterion and the conclusion of its first assertion.

proof.text: The common classes $C$ and $W=W_1=W_2$ have common intersection $C\cap W$, so the two weak factorization systems $(C\cap W,F_i)$ have the same left class. Each right class is exactly $(C\cap W)^{\square}$, giving $F_1=F_2$. Their trivial cofibrations are $C\cap W$ and their trivial fibrations are $F_i\cap W$, hence both trivial classes agree.

source.place: Proposition E.1.10, determination of the model structure; recovery of F from the model weak factorization systems.

proof.text: For a fixed adjunction $L\dashv R$ involving $\mathcal M$ and a fixed other model category, being Quillen means that $L$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations, equivalently that $R$ preserves fibrations and trivial fibrations. These predicates are identical by Steps 1, 4, and 5. For a Quillen adjunction, being a Quillen equivalence means that for every cofibrant object $A$ of its source, every fibrant object $B$ of its target, and every map $LA\to B$, that map is a weak equivalence if and only if its adjunct $A\to RB$ is. Both the objects quantified over and both weak-equivalence predicates are identical after replacing either occurrence of a model structure on $\mathcal M$. Thus the Quillen-equivalence predicate is identical as well.

source.place: Definitions in Appendix E.2 of Quillen pair and Quillen equivalence; consequences of equality of model classes.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NI-f522f8459 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Six steps checked. (1) The trivial fibrations are the common right class C^⧄ and the cofibrant objects are common; no premature claim about trivial cofibrations. (2) The cofibrant-replacement lifting square gives q_B u0 = u q_A, and 2-of-3 reduces u to u0. (3) The very good cylinders are common to both structures, and the lift k is well-posed because p_QB j_QB(u0⊔u0) = u0 p_QA j_QA, so precomposition descends to the quotients. (4) The new detector is applied to u0, with every hypothesis verified, giving W1=W2. (5) F_i = (C∩W)^⧄. (6) The Quillen and Quillen-equivalence predicates agree. New node lem-coef-fixed-cylinder-fibrant-target-detection: true (fixed-cylinder transfer, Joyal E.1.8 representability, Yoneda, E.1.4 saturation); tested on the trivial model structure and on Kan ∅→Δ0 and ∂Δ1→Δ1.
